description: Default::default() for ValidationPolicy sets current_time_unix=0 (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z). Any cert with notBefore > 0 (i.e. every cert issued after 1970) will fail check_validity with ValidityPeriod. The inline comment says 'caller must set to avoid silent clock skew' but this is in the implementation, not the rustdoc on the field. A caller who uses ValidationPolicy { max_path_len: 5, ..Default::default() } and forgets to set current_time_unix will get spurious ValidityPeriod errors with no indication the time was never set. The rustdoc on current_time_unix should prominently warn that 0 causes all validity checks to fail, and the Default impl should document this explicitly in a # Panics or # Warning rustdoc section. Consider using Option<u64> with None meaning 'skip validity check' or requiring callers to construct the policy without Default.
title: ValidationPolicy::default() sets current_time_unix=0 causing silent failure
